title: 2013 AMC 10A 23
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB = 86,\) and \(AC=97.\) A circle with center \(A\) and radius \(AB\) intersects \(\overline{BC}\) at points \(B\) and \(X.\) Moreover \(\overline{BX}\) and \(\overline{CX}\) have integer lengths. What is \(BC?\)

solutions.text:
By power of a point from \(C\), \(CB\cdot CX\) \(=AC^2-AB^2\) \(=97^2-86^2\).

This equals \((97-86)(97+86)\) \(=11\cdot183\) \(=2013\) \(=3\cdot11\cdot61\).

Both \(CX\) and \(BX\) are integers, so \(BC=BX+CX\) is an integer factor paired with \(CX\). Also \(CX<BC<86+97=183\), so the only possible pair is \(CX=33\), \(BC=61\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Use power of a point from \(C\)
Factor \(AC^2-AB^2\) and use the triangle inequality to choose the valid factor pair
